policy.title: Benchmark evidence policy
policy.summary: Benchmarks are supporting evidence, not our final ranking. We identify the exact model/version, source, snapshot date and harness. Product scores are not treated as model scores, and results from different harness versions are not compared directly.

sources.name: Arena Text Leaderboard
sources.measures: Human preference in anonymous model-vs-model battles across open-ended text tasks.
sources.caveat: A product such as ChatGPT or Claude can change its default model; Arena ranks specific model versions, not the whole product. Checked 2026-09-14 and re-checked 2026-09-21, 2026-09-28, 2026-10-05, 2026-10-12, 2026-10-19, 2026-10-26, 2026-11-09, 2026-11-16 and 2026-11-23: /leaderboard/text 308-redirects to /leaderboard/chat/text, which answers a Cloudflare managed challenge to plain HTTP clients (HTTP 403) and to a headless Chrome DOM dump, so this check again read the board through a persistent Chrome profile (Playwright driving the installed Chrome channel with an automation-hiding init script) and cross-read the rendered rows against the page's own embedded per-model JSON (rank, rating, confidence bounds, vote count and modelKey). The board served a new snapshot dated 2026-11-22 (9,241,799 votes, 427 models), replacing the 2026-11-11 snapshot (9,122,174 votes, 421 models). The snapshot re-keyed every listing - model keys now carry a four-character suffix (for example grok-4.1-xv3g) and hyphenated version numbers became dotted (claude-sonnet-4.5-...) - so the six tracked rows were re-identified by display name and organisation instead of by their old key. No rating moved at integer rounding, but every tracked rank fell and votes fell on all six, on a board whose total rose by 119,625. Newer same-board listings were again seen and deliberately NOT added as rows: grok-4.5 (#59, 1465.61, 38,965 votes), grok-4.1-thinking (#60, 1465.36, 65,914 votes) and deepseek-v4-pro-high-20260813 (#65, 1463.60, 9,529 votes). This registry carries one representative exact listing per product family, and the site's generators key rows by tool_slug, so a second row for the same family would silently overwrite the first in every generated comparison rather than adding evidence.

sources.name: Arena-Rank methodology
sources.measures: Bradley-Terry ratings with reweighting and confidence intervals from pairwise preference data.
sources.use_for: Explaining how Arena scores are produced
sources.caveat: Human preference can reward style and verbosity; it is not an objective factuality test.

sources.name: SWE-bench Verified
sources.measures: Percentage of 500 human-validated real GitHub issues resolved by a coding model or agent.
sources.caveat: Scores depend heavily on the agent harness. mini-SWE-agent v1.x and v2.x results are not directly comparable. Checked 2026-09-21 and re-checked 2026-09-28, 2026-10-05, 2026-10-12, 2026-10-19, 2026-10-26, 2026-11-09, 2026-11-16 and 2026-11-23: the site still publishes a machine-readable results payload on the home page (an embedded leaderboard-data JSON block covering Multilingual, Test, Verified, Lite and Multimodal). The Verified group is unchanged at 180 rows dated 2023-10-10 to 2026-02-26; the newest is still a mini-SWE-agent 2.0.0 run on Gemini 3 Pro at 69.6% resolved, and the highest score in the group is Sonar Foundation Agent + Claude 4.5 Opus at 79.2% (2025-12-05), tied by live-SWE-agent + Claude 4.5 Opus medium at 79.2% (2025-12-15). No Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Replit, Windsurf or Devin product appears in that Verified set - the only Devin-substring occurrence is an OpenHands folder named 20240725_opendevin_codeact_v1.8_claude35sonnet in the Lite group - so no product-level coding row is added from it. The page text still confirms the 500-instance human-validated subset.

sources.name: LiveBench
sources.measures: Objective, frequently refreshed tasks across reasoning, math, coding, language, instruction following and data analysis.
sources.caveat: Always state the release; questions and model configurations change between snapshots. Checked 2026-09-21 and re-checked 2026-09-28, 2026-10-05, 2026-10-12, 2026-10-19, 2026-10-26, 2026-11-09, 2026-11-16 and 2026-11-23: the repository is live (latest commit still 2026-10-18, adding a deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-max configuration), but its own changelog.md still ends at 2026-01-08 and the README still shows "Top models as of 30th September 2024". The material content sits on the website, which is branded "LiveBench 2.0 - a challenging, contamination-free long-horizon AI benchmark" and whose bundled release list now ends at a new 2026-11-06 release (/data/20261106/table.csv, HTTP 200, 35 model rows), followed by 2026-10-25 (/data/20261025/table.csv, 32 model rows) and 2026-10-14 (/data/20261014/table.csv, 55 model rows), all across the same seven categories (long_agentic, reasoning, coding, browser, data_analysis, research, design). No release dated after 2026-11-06 exists (probed the 2026-11-01, 2026-11-08, 2026-11-09, 2026-11-12, 2026-11-14, 2026-11-15 and 2026-11-16 table paths, all 404). Generation v1 releases run 2024-06-24 through 2026-06-25. The two generations use different task sets and must never be pooled or compared, and neither is a product-level ranking: no registry row is scored from LiveBench, which is used as contamination-limited model context only.

sources.name: Artificial Analysis methodology
sources.measures: Independent intelligence, latency, speed, price, speech, image and video model evaluations.
sources.use_for: Cost/speed context and non-text modality methodology
sources.caveat: API model measurements do not equal the complete end-user product experience. Checked 2026-09-21 and re-checked 2026-09-28, 2026-10-05, 2026-10-12, 2026-10-19, 2026-10-26, 2026-11-09, 2026-11-16 and 2026-11-23: the methodology page is live (HTTP 200, 330,528 bytes, title "Artificial Analysis Benchmarking Methodology") and still serves no dated per-model score table (zero <table> elements), so no Artificial Analysis row exists in this registry.

sources.name: Terminal-Bench leaderboard (frozen 2.1 URL now serves 4.1)
sources.measures: Accuracy of an agent + model + reasoning-effort configuration on 89 complex containerized terminal tasks.
sources.use_for: Coding agents and terminal-capable development tools
sources.caveat: Checked 2026-09-14, re-checked 2026-09-21, 2026-09-28, 2026-10-05, 2026-10-12, 2026-10-19, 2026-10-26, 2026-11-09, 2026-11-16 and 2026-11-23: https://www.tbench.ai/leaderboard/terminal-bench/2.1 still returns a 308 redirect to https://www.tbench.ai/?version=2.1, and that route does not serve the 2.1 or 4.0 board - the host now serves Terminal-Bench 4.1 (leaderboard slug "4-1-0", title "Terminal-Bench 4.1", created 2026-11-03, updated_at 2026-11-20T16:07:10Z, 67 rows at 330 trials each, and no other board in the page payload). The 4.1 board now carries its first GitHub Copilot entry - GitHub Copilot CLI + "Copilot Fusion" at max effort, 71.2% +/-2.9 over 330 trials, dated 2026-11-17, which is the current #1 - so the earlier statement that the board had zero Copilot, Cursor, Windsurf or Replit entries no longer holds; there is still no Cursor, Windsurf or Replit entry. The rest of the board is Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity CLI, Grok Build, Muse Code and mini-SWE-agent configurations, with Claude Code + Opus 5.5 max effort (65.8% +/-3.1, 2026-09-22) and Claude Code + Fable 5.2 max effort (65.8% +/-2.8, 2026-11-09) next. No 2.1 rows can be read from this URL on any date and no archived 2.1 board is reachable, so nothing here can move the registry's 2.1 Cursor coding row; the new GitHub Copilot result is NOT added as a row because the site's cursor-vs-github-copilot page keys rows by tool_slug and would then place a 4.1 result beside a 2.1 result. 2.1, 4.0 and 4.1 are different harness versions and are not comparable with each other. Never present this as a model-only score; keep agent, exact model, effort, trial count and integrity metadata visible.

sources.name: Artificial Analysis Image methodology
sources.measures: Blind pairwise image preference with exact model/version and matched prompt conditions.
sources.caveat: Keep text-to-image and editing pools separate; old model versions are historical evidence only. Checked 2026-09-21 and re-checked 2026-09-28, 2026-10-05, 2026-10-12, 2026-10-19, 2026-10-26, 2026-11-09, 2026-11-16 and 2026-11-23: the page resolves at https://artificialanalysis.ai/methodology/image (HTTP 200, 395,133 bytes, title "Image Generation Benchmarking Methodology"), keeps separate text-to-image and editing sections, and serves no dated score table (zero <table> elements).

sources.name: Artificial Analysis Video methodology
sources.measures: Modality-separated video quality, latency and price comparisons.
sources.caveat: Do not compare Elo across different video modalities or output settings. Checked 2026-09-21 and re-checked 2026-09-28, 2026-10-05, 2026-10-12, 2026-10-19, 2026-10-26, 2026-11-09, 2026-11-16 and 2026-11-23: the page resolves at https://artificialanalysis.ai/methodology/video (HTTP 200, 444,822 bytes) and still states that each modality has its own Elo pool in the Video Arena, so silent and audio-enabled outputs are not compared directly and editing is not compared with generation. Its only <table> is the settings/parameters table (1080p, 24 FPS, 10 s, 16:9, seed 42); no dated score table is served.

sources.name: Artificial Analysis TTS methodology
sources.measures: Provider-voice and controlled-voice human-preference comparisons for text-to-speech.
sources.caveat: Controlled-voice and provider-voice arenas answer different questions and must remain separate. Checked 2026-09-21 and re-checked 2026-09-28, 2026-10-05, 2026-10-12, 2026-10-19, 2026-10-26, 2026-11-09, 2026-11-16 and 2026-11-23: the page resolves at https://artificialanalysis.ai/methodology/text-to-speech (HTTP 200, 473,459 bytes, title "Text to Speech Benchmarking Methodology"), separates the provider-voice and controlled-voice sections, and serves no dated score table (zero <table> elements).

sources.name: Terminal-Bench: Cursor CLI + Grok 4.5 submission
sources.measures: Maintainer-verified Terminal-Bench 2.1 submission record for one exact Cursor CLI configuration.
sources.caveat: Checked 2026-09-14, re-checked 2026-09-21, re-hashed 2026-09-28, 2026-10-05, 2026-10-12, 2026-10-19, 2026-10-26, 2026-11-09, 2026-11-16 and 2026-11-23 against the raw submission file (sha256 a73454861c91299b501637e6df6082f2f16cf9c9f6c98f07bce315189f82eb23, 29,033 bytes, byte-identical on every check): Cursor CLI 2026.07.08-0c04a8a + cursor/grok-4.5 at high effort, 79.33% +/- 1.46, 445 trials, 8.99% reward-hack disqualifications, dated 2026-07-09. Two limits sit on it: the Terminal-Bench 2.1 README states "Community submissions are currently closed for Terminal-Bench 2.1", so the 2.1 board is frozen, and neither the later 4.0 board nor the current 4.1 board (updated 2026-11-20) carries a Cursor entry, so there is no newer Cursor reading to compare it to. Scores from 2.1, 4.0 and 4.1 are different harness versions and must never be compared with each other.

sources.name: Harbor Hub — Terminal-Bench 2.1 dataset
sources.measures: The live dataset record for Terminal-Bench 2.1: which tasks the frozen board ran and which version is published.
sources.use_for: Confirming the task set behind a Terminal-Bench 2.1 configuration score
sources.caveat: Checked 2026-09-14, re-checked 2026-09-21, 2026-09-28, 2026-10-05, 2026-10-12, 2026-10-19, 2026-10-26, 2026-11-09, 2026-11-16 and 2026-11-23: the dataset page still describes "Version 2.1 of Terminal-Bench" and still serves revision 6 (package version 2.0.2, tagged latest) as its latest published revision, out of six revisions (1.0.0 through 2.0.2). The Terminal-Bench 2.1 repository independently holds 91 task entries at main (89 task directories after README.md and dataset.toml), matching the 89 tasks this dataset reports. The upstream Terminal-Bench repository now publishes three release tags - v4.1.0, v4.0.0 and v3.0.0 - and both v4.1.0 and v4.0.0 hold 68 task entries (66 task directories), so 4.x is not a "larger" task set than 2.1 either: 2.1, 4.0 and 4.1 are different task sets, not a small/large pair. A separate 4.1 dataset page now also resolves on this host (terminal-bench-4-1, HTTP 200). This page publishes the task list, not leaderboard scores; it cannot upgrade a 2.1 score into a 4.0 or 4.1 score.
